prize_parts.citation: For the theoretical prediction of flat electronic bands at magic twist angles in bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

statement.case_for: I moved B001 from fourth place on my opening ballot to my preferred configuration after reading the other seven ballots. The Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum model is a concrete prediction made in 2011 that was tested seven years later, and the 2018 correlated-insulator and superconducting results of the Jarillo-Herrero group opened a field of tunable correlated matter that has since spread to twisted multilayers, transition-metal dichalcogenides and fractional Chern insulators. Four of eight members placed it first, five placed it in their top three, and all eight ranked it. That breadth matters because the members come from different subfields. The physics is reproduced by many independent groups and the core discovery does not depend on resolving the mechanism of the superconductivity. The theory-plus-experiment split into MacDonald and Bistritzer on one side and Jarillo-Herrero on the other is as clean as these attribution problems get.
statement.case_against: Attribution to the experiment is thin with only one experimental name. The 2018 papers had co-authors, notably Yuan Cao as first author, and other groups reported related correlated states quickly, so the three-person limit forces a hard choice that the committee must defend. The field is also still moving fast and the origin of the superconductivity is unresolved, so a sceptic can say the lasting content is not yet fixed. Finally, my own field is not represented in this configuration. I ranked circuit QED first on my opening ballot, and only I gave it that rank, so I must separate my interest from the merits and not argue for B058 against the weight of the committee.

responses.point: B001 is a clean prediction followed by an experimental test, which a theorist can respect, and eight years is neither premature nor late.
responses.response: I agree on the structure and on the timing, and that is what moved me. I would add one qualification. The prediction-then-test story is cleanest for the flat-band magic angle but weaker for the superconducting phase, where theory still lags the data. So the citation should credit the prediction of the flat bands and the discovery of the correlated and superconducting states, and it should not claim an explanation of the superconductivity.

responses.point: A two-person prize for MacDonald and Jarillo-Herrero is the cleanest configuration, although it would leave Bistritzer out.
responses.response: I disagree with dropping Bistritzer. The 2011 paper is a joint Bistritzer-MacDonald result, and the continuum model that predicts the magic angle carries both names in the literature. Deleting one of two authors of the decisive theory to gain tidiness is a poor reason when the three-person limit allows the full pair. I would rather keep three names and accept the experimental thinness than make the theory credit incomplete.

responses.point: Optical lattice clocks (B007) are the clearest case of an invention that changed what can be measured, with strong independent confirmation and a pending redefinition of the second.
responses.response: I think B007 is a very strong candidate and I rank it as my first alternative. I did not choose it first because I find the twisted-bilayer case a rarer example of a prediction later confirmed, and because it drew more first-place votes across a broader set of subfields. I note that a two-part prize joining B001 and B007 would need five names, which breaks the three-person limit. I would resist cutting names from either to make that fit. If the committee judges that B001 is not yet settled, B007 is where I would turn.

responses.point: B001 is a rare case where a relatively simple theory predicted a phenomenon, with the tuning of interaction strength by geometry being the new element, and the Cao and Dean experimental groups are possible further names.
responses.response: I share the view on the physics. On Dean and others, I would like to hear whether you think the experimental credit should be widened at the cost of a theorist. I would not, because the 2011 prediction and the 2018 discovery are the two decisive steps and a prize can credit the field's origin without naming every group. I would keep the three names.

responses.point: Aberration-corrected electron optics (B030) broke the Scherzer barrier and is now ubiquitous in materials physics, though recognition may be overdue.
responses.response: The impact on materials physics is not in doubt and I take the point that it is a clearly defined invention. My reservation is about discovery versus instrumentation. The prize should go to something that changed the physical knowledge we hold, and the corrector mostly improved the way we see it. I do not rank it as an alternative, but I would listen if you want to make the case that the field-wide enabling effect is the criterion.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a single experimental name for B001, or will want to widen the experimental credit beyond Jarillo-Herrero within the three-person limit.
Whether the unresolved mechanism of superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene makes the discovery look provisional.
How much weight the 2025 circuit prize should put against B058, and whether Andreas Wallraff, who is not among the credited names for B058, would need to be added.
Whether a different configuration with B007 as a second part is feasible, given that the combined list of names would exceed three.
statement.conflict_note: I direct WACQT and work at Chalmers in superconducting circuits and quantum computing, so B058 (circuit QED) and, less directly, B015 are in my own field. I have worked with Chalmers colleagues Per Delsing and C. M. Wilson and with Anton Frisk Kockum, and Chalmers hosted researchers connected to the 2025 prize. None of the people credited for B001 or B007 appears in my profile as a collaborator, but I would recuse myself from any discussion that centres on B058 beyond giving field-specific information. I cannot identify other specific conflicts from my profile.
